definition: Perfunctory means done as a routine duty with minimal effort and no real interest or enthusiasm — carried out just to get it over with.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word perfunctory. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know perfunctory should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The guard gave the badges a perfunctory glance, waving through anyone who held up something laminated.
Cursory is milder than perfunctory: a cursory reading at least races through the whole text with intent, while a perfunctory one has stopped caring whether anything registers.
Token goes beyond perfunctory: a perfunctory inspection is still an inspection, done without interest, but a token one exists only so the paperwork can say it happened.
Cursory means hasty and skipping the details, usually because time is short; perfunctory adds indifference — there was time enough, but no interest in using it.
Halfhearted means done with little energy because the doer's heart isn't in it; halfhearted still admits a trace of trying, while perfunctory is pure box-checking — form observed, effort withheld.
Automatic means happening without conscious thought, like a reflex; perfunctory acts are chosen — the person could engage with the task, and doesn't.

Perfunctory means done as a routine duty with minimal effort and no real interest or enthusiasm — carried out just to get it over with.

Asked at the press conference about the outgoing minister, the premier offered a perfunctory tribute — two sentences of boilerplate thanks, read off a card — before turning eagerly to the next question.
The duty was technically met: a tribute was delivered.
But the flat routine of it — no interest, no enthusiasm, no glance up from the card — is exactly what perfunctory names.
The eager turn to the next question proves the energy existed; it just wasn't spent here.
Perfunctory is an observer's verdict on effort, not on results — a perfunctory inspection can pass a safe bridge and still deserve the adjective.
It attaches best to small performed rituals: nods, applause, apologies, glances.
When speed is the point and interest is beside it, reach for cursory instead.

Okafor's hotel inspections had been feared; lately they had become perfunctory.
He still arrived precisely at nine, still carried the famous clipboard, and still visited every floor in the old order.
But managers noticed that he no longer ran a finger along the doorframes, and that the boxes on his form were ticked in smooth unbroken runs, sometimes before a door was opened.
He was not rushed — the tours took as long as ever — and he was not unkind.
The routine simply continued without him inside it, and the hotels, one by one, quietly stopped being afraid.
